option_relations.rationale: Acute on Chronic Liver Failure (ACLF) is a clinical syndrome, not a specific disease entity like Hepatitis C Virus infection. While HCV can cause ACLF, ACLF itself is not equivalent to HCV infection.

Acute-on-chronic liver failure due to acute hepatitis C virus infection describes a clinical syndrome with an etiology, but it is not equivalent to the leaf 'Hepatitis C Virus (HCV) infection' which is the underlying disease.
The option 'Hepatitis C virus infection' is clinically equivalent to the leaf 'Hepatitis C Virus (HCV) infection'.
Acute Hepatitis C Virus (HCV) Infection is a specific subtype or stage of the broader 'Hepatitis C Virus (HCV) infection'.
